lines.text: Almeda Genoa Road. The lot's closed, and the lamps are still on.
Evening. Lot's closed, but the lamps stay on a while.
If you're after the man in the green suit, he's by the showroom.
Rain's the only customer that never haggles.
Go on. Mind the puddles. They're deeper than they look.
Tonight I do. I lock the gate and keep the rain off the windshields.
Mostly the rain wins.
Nobody's expecting anybody this late. Go say hello.
Showroom's that way. Follow the lamps.
This gate and I have an understanding. It doesn't move, and neither do I.
Well, look at that. Thank you. Go on in before you drown.
Clear vehicles. Clear terms. Real people. Somebody painted that and meant it.
A board of sold tags by the door. Somebody keeps count.
Rain beads on the hood like it was waxed this afternoon.
The lamps hang upside down in the puddles, waiting for somebody to step on them.
Hi. I'm fictional, before you ask. So are my numbers.
Still fictional. Still happy with the deal.
Signed. That was quick. Thank you, fictionally.
Least painful thing that's happened to me all week.
Thanks for calling Triple J Auto. How can I help?
Hi. Is the gray truck on your site still there? Could I come see it Saturday?
It's still here. I can book you for Saturday morning. What's your name?
Marcus.
You're all booked, Marcus. See you Saturday.
One more thing. Can you hold the truck if I put money down tonight?
That's one for the team. Let me get someone for you.
Folders tabbed by hand. Form 130-U, webDEALER, liens, temp tags.
A data model in marker. Lead, deal, title. Three notes hang off it.
A lead from Facebook Marketplace, researched and waiting. The seller's labelled example.
A ledger, closed. The kind you keep even when the computer keeps it too.
An arcade cabinet. After Hours: The Run. Somebody turned a resume into a game.
The coffee machine ticks as it cools.
From in here the lot looks like a painting of itself.
The library will close soon. Please bring your books to the front desk.
The desk lamp hums. The rest of the floor has gone dark.
Morning. Dry asphalt. The lamps are off for once.
A waiting room, late. The clock is loud. Nobody here wants to be here.
He hasn't looked up since you sat down.
Missed calls from the lot. People asking about cars.
It's buzzing again.
Hi. Is the silver one on the lot still for sale?
Somebody still needs a car. The world doesn't wait.
It rings out. It'll ring again in the morning.
Rain on the glass. The parking lights blur into one.
Bad coffee from the machine. You hand him one anyway.
Somewhere past midnight, he's the one who stands up first.
The next morning. The lot in daylight. A buyer by the first car.
I'm just looking. I've been burned before.
Everybody tells me about the car.
So it was overpriced?
The last car broke down a week after I bought it. Nobody answered the phone.
Can I drive it?
It drives right. I'll take it.
She drives off. He watches until the car turns the corner.
Thanks again for the gate. Get home safe.
Somebody's bell. It still rings like it's new.
A cold bench. The rain keeps its own schedule here.
Bus stop. Nobody's waiting tonight.
A book left open on the cart, like someone meant to come back.
A chair by the desk. It takes the weight of a long day.
Cold water over the shoes. Worth it.
The lamp clicks on. The room gets smaller and warmer.
Pens, spare tags, a ring of keys. Every desk has a drawer like this.
The lid bangs down louder than you meant it to.
A cold light and not much else.
Ice, packed tight. Somebody fills it every morning.
Locked. The pumps stand around in the rain.
Warm air and the smell of dryer sheets.
Laundry. Open late. Somebody always is.
The lamps break apart under your feet, then come back together.
Empty. Whatever came today is already inside.
Still warm. Somebody was here a minute ago.
Yesterday's paper, damp at the corners.
The lights buzz once and settle.
A dial tone. Nobody to call, but it still works.
Low music, mostly static. Enough to keep the room company.
The long tables come up out of the dark.
Nobody home. The rain answers instead.
The shutter rattles all the way down the block.
Closed. Most of the street is, this late.
Your own reflection knocks back.
The showroom wakes up, one row at a time.
Tacos. Open late. The best kind of sign.
The bell dings over the hiss of the grill.
Something drops with a thunk. Small victories.
